newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels move on copper-rich region.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels move on copper-rich region.

text.p: Zairean rebels consolidated their advance on Thursday on the southeastern town of Moba in mineral-rich Shaba province, and appealed to Moroccan King Hassan to ignore a Zairean request for military aid.
"We are consolidating our advance on Moba. We are also spreading our forces around the town," said an official at rebel headquarters in this lakeside city.

The advance on Moba follows the capture of the mining port town of Kalemie on Lake Tanganyika and is a strategic move by rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), seeking control of the politically significant Shaba region.
Shaba is the mining centre of Zaire's copper and cobalt deposits -- the third largest in the world.

Rebel officals said the embattled government in Kinshasa was pouring military reinforcements into Moba by air and railway from the nearby Kamina base -- built by the United States in the 1970s and used as a staging post for operations against Cuban and Soviet forces in neighbouring Angola.
But the ADFL leader and commander-in-chief, Laurent Kabila, said the reinforcements had come "too late" and would not stop his guerrilla force from capturing the town.
"Mobutu has no army. We shall deal with the reinforcements being sent (into Moba).We shall defeat them," Kabila told Reuters.
Kabila's radio station in Goma broadcast an appeal to King Hassan of Morocco requesting him to ignore a request for military aid from ailing Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko, a longtime ally.

"The government of the Democratic Congo appeals to King Hassan to ignore requests by Marshal Mobutu for military aid to help him in the people's war against dictatorship," said the broadcast in the local Swahili language.
"We will continue to fight local or foreign forces seeking to support Mobutu against the people's will," it added.

Mobutu, in power for 31 years which have left the vast mineral-rich country at the heart of Africa one of the world's poorest, is visiting Morocco for talks with King Hassan. Officials say military aid for his ragged army is high on the agenda.
Officials say Mobutu is keen to match the ADFL's rapid training programme of thousands of young men and women who have enlisted in the vast area the rebels control.
On Thursday, Kabila is to officiate at a graduation parade for 5,000 ADFL soldiers in Goma before they are dispatched to the rapidly expanding frontline in Africa's newest war.

Kabila said his army, which has scored stunning battlefield successes since he launched a military campaign last October, was also pushing forward towards Lubutu, home to Rwanda's ousted 40,000-strong army and more than 100,000 Hutu refugees.

Kabila said his forces were within 19 km (11 miles) of Lubutu after capturing a key bridge leading to the town. He said a fierce battle for the bridge lasted several days and his forces shot down helicopters brought in to reinforce pinned-down government troops and their Rwandan Hutu allies.
He said some 7,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees had crosed over to his forces at the town of Walikale and his forces were now preparing to repatriate them to their tiny central African nation.

Kabila said he was ready to open up corridors for more than 100,000 Randan Hutus trapped in camps around Kisangani and Lubutu and appealed to the U.N. refugee agency to approach him so that arrangements could be worked out.

The fall of Lubutu would leave Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city after Kinshasa and Lubumbashi, vulnerable to Kabila's forces and analysts predict it would trigger general panic across Africa's second largest country.
Kisangani is also currently Zaire's key military operational centre where mercenaries -- said by Kabila to number 300 -- have gathered in preparation for a push against the rebels.

Kabila said his forces were also besieging government forces at Shabunda, home to 35,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, at Kindu, a major airbase, and outside the town of Watsa captured by his troops five days ago.
